key_insight: DocTalk improved chart-grounded medical question answering through clinically aligned LoRA instruction tuning of open-source language models.
clinical_relevance: The system could help clinicians retrieve information from discharge summaries, though improved QA scores do not establish clinical safety or patient benefit.
method: Generated 500 QA pairs from de-identified discharge summaries using sentence-level decomposition, chain-of-thought-guided question formulation, and expert review.
Evaluated six general-purpose and biomedical LLMs before and after LoRA instruction tuning.
Tested the two leading models on PubMedQA and deployed an interactive EHR-querying web platform.
evidence_signal: The best tuned model achieved ROUGE-L 0.40, BERTScore-F1 0.76, and UMLS-F1 0.49; PubMedQA accuracy rose from 93.1% to 97.7% and from 93.5% to 94.3% for the two leading models.
watch_item: The 500-pair dataset and benchmark gains do not establish reliability in real-world clinical workflows; prospective safety validation remains necessary.
paper_title: DocTalk: Enhancing Medical Knowledge Retrieval via Fine-tuned Large Language Models with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Robust Clinical Decision Support
